title: GKE Standard: node pools, upgrades and maintenance windows

videos.script: A managed cluster sounds like somebody else's problem. Half of it is. This lesson is about the half that stays yours. {{control}} Google runs the control plane. You never see its machines, and you pay a flat fee for it. One cluster's fee is about seventy-three dollars a month. {{pools}} The nodes are yours. They come in pools of identical machines. In a regional cluster, a node count of one means one in every zone. That surprise is the first line of many GKE bills. {{upgrades}} Then upgrades. Google picks the versions through a release channel. Your nodes are replaced one by one, with your pods on them. You decide how many at a time. {{windows}} Last, you decide when. A maintenance window keeps upgrades at two in the morning. An exclusion keeps them out of your busiest week. Neither keeps a cluster still forever.
